title: State of the World and Russia
description:
State of World
	Industrial Revolution
	Uprising in France
	Colonial wars
	New thought schools
		Liberal
		Radical
		Conservative
	New social structure
		Republicanism
		Capitalism
		Socialism
			Robert Owen (UK): Cooperative agriculture, industrial communities
			Louis Blanc (France): From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs; Government should encourage cooperatives
			Karl Marx (Germany): Capitalism was root cause of all evils
		Communism
		Monopoly
	Formation of socialist (labour) parties all over Europe and world
	Socialist international organisation: The Second International
	In many countries, socialist parties were fighting elections or in power

State in Russia
	Economic structure
		Agriculture sector
			Majority agriculture unorganised
			Land pooling and redistribution of produce
			Land owning peasants pooled land and redistributed produce
			Landless peasants were paid meagre salaries and exploited
			Landlords were harsh and worked with novelty
		Industrial sector
			Foreign capital
			Industry in towns (Petersburg, Moscow)
			Labour exploitation
			Poor labour laws
			Low wages
			Difficult working conditions
			Women and child labour preferred
			Labour classification by dress and caste
	Social and political system
		Tsar: ruling class
		Clergy and nobility owned large lands
		Peasants owned lands
		Landless peasants earned wages
		Agricultural workers
		Industrial workers
		Army soldiers had little land and low share of produce

title: Bloody Sunday and 1905 Revolution
description:
People came to Tsar for help
	1.15 lakh people with Father Gapon submitted memorandum to Tsar
	2.Guards shot and killed 300 people (Bloody Sunday)
	3.Protests across the nation; whole system and industries halted
	4.Soviets and liberals joined protests
	5.Tsar accepted losing power and issued October Manifesto
	October Manifesto
		i.Creation of Duma
		ii.Civil rights for citizens

title: Abolition of Duma I
description: First Duma was abolished by Tsar

title: Abolition of Duma II
description: Second Duma was abolished by Tsar

title: February Revolution
description:
Strike in Russia
	High inflation and food shortage caused women to strike
	Petrograd city; slogan: Down with aristocracy
	1.5 lakh men and women joined next day (Women's Day)
	Tsar removed from throne
	Duma III formed provisional government
	Good policies
		Abolished death penalty
		Amnesty to political prisoners and exiles
		Ended religious and ethnic discrimination
		Granted civil rights
		Adult suffrage
	Bad policies
		Did not end war
		Did not improve living conditions
		Did not perform land reforms

title: Lenin Returns
description:
Lenin returns from exile
	Slogan: Peace, Land, Bread
	April Theses
		End of war
		Nationalisation of all banks
		Return of land to peasants

title: October Revolution
description:
Decision of revolution
	Bolshevik Party planned overthrow
	Military Revolutionary Committee under Leon Trotsky
	Lenin seized power
	Alexander Kerensky removed
	Russia withdrew from war
	Banks and industries nationalised
	Tsar, nobles and church lands given to peasants
	Houses distributed
	Foreign investment confiscated
	Public utilities nationalised
	Bolshevik party renamed Communist Party

title: One Party Rule
description:
Assembly rejected Bolshevik policies
	Lenin dismissed assembly
	All Russian Congress became parliament
	Russia became one-party democracy
	Economic conditions
		Soldiers returned and wanted jobs
		More people in towns caused food shortage
		Less agricultural production
		No new foreign investment
		Industries not hiring; low wages and low demand

title: Civil War Begins
description:
Civil war groups
	White: Conservatives wanted Tsar back
	Red: Bolsheviks wanted to remain in power
	Green: Liberals wanted peace
	Greens joined Whites and took control of most Russia
	Reds were losing and joined Muslim Jedidests

title: Formation of USSR
description:
Soviet Union formed
	Union of Soviet Socialist Republics came into existence

title: Stalin and Five Year Plans
description:
Joseph Stalin becomes leader
	Five-year plans introduced
	Gosplan created
	Collectivisation started
		Collective farms (Kolkhoz)
		State farms (Sovkhoz)
		Kulaks (wealthy peasants)
	Kulaks raided
	Political repression continued
	International impact
		Spread of communism
		Communist parties formed globally
		International communist unions
		State-led planning
		Improved dignity of labour
		End of imperialism
		Rise of nationalism in Asia and Africa
		World divided into socialist and capitalist

title: Collapse of USSR
description:
USSR breaks down
	Newly formed countries create CIS (Commonwealth of Independent States)
